title: Topside Roast Beef
subtitle: Slow-roasted lean joint with pan gravy
excerpt: Topside cooked at a low temperature for even doneness and sliced thinly against the grain. A leaner Sunday roast than rib of beef, best served medium-rare with its own pan juices and horseradish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Topside is a lean cut from the inner hind leg of beef, cheaper than rib and sirloin. It has long been a British Sunday roast staple because of its relatively low price and good yield. Because it has very little intramuscular fat, it benefits from low-temperature cooking and frequent basting, or it will dry out. Resting is essential to redistribute the juices.

recipeTools.notes: Large roasting tin with a rack if possible.

content.text: Topside needs two things: a hot blast at the start to colour the outside, then a lower temperature for the rest of the cook. Take it out of the fridge a full hour before roasting so the centre is not cold when it goes into the oven. Rest it for at least 20 minutes before carving; topside is lean and the juices will run out if you cut it too soon. Aim for 55 to 57 C internal for medium-rare.

Heat the oven to 240 C / fan 220 C / gas 9. Rub the beef all over with oil, salt, and pepper. Put the onion, garlic, and rosemary in the base of the roasting tin. Set the beef on top. Roast for 20 minutes to colour the outside.

Reduce the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Roast for a further 50 to 60 minutes, basting every 20 minutes, until a thermometer reads 55 C for medium-rare or 60 C for medium. Transfer to a board and rest, loosely covered with foil, for 20 to 30 minutes.

Make the gravy: pour off most of the fat from the tin, leaving 2 tablespoons. Place the tin over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine, scrape the pan, then add the stock. Simmer for 8 minutes until thickened. Strain and season.
Carve the beef thinly against the grain. Serve with the gravy, horseradish, roast potatoes, and greens.
